# Git workflow

## Strategy

We worked in a public GitHub repository, with `main` as the reference branch. We created the `.gitignore` before working together, and it was completed when needed. It excludes temporary RStudio and Quarto files, as well as rendered HTML files.

We used a master document, `IEAP-Series04-Rstudio.qmd`, which includes one sub-document per part. Each person mainly worked in their own file and branch, which reduced the risk of merge conflicts:

| Part                          | Person | Branch                  |
|-------------------------------|--------|-------------------------|
| Problem 1: effect of noise    | Zoé    | `problem1`              |
| Literature and 3h10 recording | Gaia   | `problem2-3h`           |
| 7m30 recording                | Jeanne | `problem2-7m`           |
| General conclusion            | Zoé    | `conclusion`            |
| Git workflow and README       | Gaia   | `git-workflow-readme`   |
| One-page PDF report           | Jeanne | — (submitted on Moodle) |

Each part was merged into `main` through a pull request, after being reviewed and approved by the other two members.

## Analysis of our work

The reviews were really useful in our work. First, it enables us to all think critically even though one person did the literature research. Indeed, the remark whether the full 161-minute period could be considered as recovery was useful to rethink our analysis by adding a clear limitation. Secondly, we spotted the errors when rendering (wrong name path and a misplaced code fence). The work was divided equally between the members of the team. The fact that the analysis was split in two instead of only one person making all the work was a good thing. Also, the fact that Zoé wrote the conclusion includes even more in the analysis of the two recordings.

We also encountered some difficulties. Because the libraries are loaded only in the master document, a sub-document could fail when run alone, so the final check must always be a render of the master document. All sub-documents are run in the same R session when the master document is rendered, so we added suffixes such as `_3h` and `_7m` to object and chunk names to avoid overwriting each other's results.

Next time, we would agree on file names and heading conventions before each working on our sub-document so we would have less modifications to do. We would also render the master document before opening each pull request to spot errors earlier.
